description: Combined PRD evidence from two isolated Codex/Ralph stream worktrees. Verification and PR gate run on this integration branch.

userStories.title: Permission request writes reject ambiguous JSON bodies
userStories.description: As an operator approving access requests, I want permission request write APIs to reject bodies containing multiple JSON values so that malformed or smuggled payloads cannot create or decide a request from only the first object.
acceptanceCriteria: Given an authenticated requester posts a valid permission request JSON object followed by another JSON value, when the request reaches POST /api/v2/permission-requests, then the API returns 400 InvalidRequestBody and no permission request is created.

Given an authenticated approver posts a valid decision note followed by another JSON value, when the request reaches POST /api/v2/permission-requests/{id}/approve, then the API returns 400 InvalidRequestBody and the permission request remains PENDING.
The BDD coverage uses the chi HTTP router and in-memory permission request store so the behavior is observable at the API boundary.
Targeted Go tests for pkg/permissionrequests pass.
dependencies: pkg/httputil.ReadJSON already enforces a single JSON value and request body size cap.

userStories.title: Tenant admin writes reject ambiguous JSON bodies
userStories.description: As a tenant administrator, I want tenant management write APIs to reject concatenated JSON bodies so that tenant state changes are parsed deterministically.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a tenant create or update request with a valid JSON object followed by another JSON value, when posted to the tenant admin API, then the API returns 400 InvalidRequestBody.
The handler does not create or mutate tenant state after rejecting the ambiguous body.
Targeted Go tests for pkg/tenants pass.
dependencies: P2A-001 establishes the narrow httputil.ReadJSON adoption pattern on one access-control write surface.

userStories.title: MCP HTTP transport rejects oversized JSON-RPC bodies
userStories.description: As an MCP client operator, I want the HTTP JSON-RPC transport to fail oversized request bodies predictably so that malformed clients cannot consume unbounded server memory.
acceptanceCriteria: Given an MCP HTTP request body larger than the configured server cap, when posted to the transport, then the response is a JSON-RPC error instead of attempting to decode the full body.
Normal-sized JSON-RPC requests continue to pass existing MCP transport tests.
Targeted Go tests for pkg/mcp pass.
dependencies: Existing MCP JSON-RPC error envelope tests in pkg/mcp.

userStories.title: Browser Search Renders API Highlight Snippets
userStories.description: As a Weave operator browsing objects, I want full-text search results to show backend highlight snippets so I can understand why each row matched without opening every object.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an object type with a title property and the operator submits full-text search
acceptanceCriteria.then: the request includes SearchObjectsRequest.highlight.fields for the searched title property, matching the OpenAPI US-235 highlight contract

acceptanceCriteria.given: the search response row contains _highlights.title snippets with <mark>...</mark>
acceptanceCriteria.when: the object table renders the result row
acceptanceCriteria.then: the matching title cell renders an actual mark element while preserving non-highlight text as text

acceptanceCriteria.given: a response row has no highlight snippets for a field
acceptanceCriteria.then: the field falls back to the existing truncated value rendering

acceptanceCriteria.when: targeted BrowserPage BDD, web typecheck, web Vitest coverage, and web build run

dependencies: Existing BrowserPage search BDD test harness

userStories.title: Browser Facets Prefer Detailed Searchable Metadata
userStories.description: As a Weave operator filtering object search results, I want facet requests to prefer properties marked searchable in detailed metadata so empty, non-indexed facet groups do not distract from useful filters.

acceptanceCriteria.when: BrowserPage builds a search request with facets
acceptanceCriteria.then: facet fields are selected from searchable string/boolean/date properties and still exclude the primary key

acceptanceCriteria.given: detailed property metadata is still loading or unavailable
acceptanceCriteria.then: the current compact-property fallback behavior remains stable

userStories.title: Saved Browser Views Restore Presentation Mode
userStories.description: As a Weave operator saving an object browser view, I want the saved definition to restore the selected table/map/gantt/sankey/pivot presentation mode along with filters and sort.

acceptanceCriteria.given: the operator saves a Browser view while a non-table mode is selected
acceptanceCriteria.when: the saved view is loaded later
acceptanceCriteria.then: BrowserPage restores that view mode and the existing filters, facets, and sort

acceptanceCriteria.given: an older saved view has no viewMode field
acceptanceCriteria.then: BrowserPage keeps the current table-mode fallback without errors
